title: Make folders and filenames match your scheme
description: Shape where filed documents land and what they're called, using the two block builders in Settings -> Files & filing: the folder builder (subfolders) and the filename builder, with the live preview updating as blocks are added or removed. NOTE: the editor is click-a-block-to-add / click-the-cross-to-remove (there is no drag-to-reorder), so the video builds the pattern rather than dragging blocks.

steps.narration: ScanFinder files every document into folders and gives it a tidy name. You decide the pattern — let's match it to how you already work.
steps.caption: Folders & filenames your way

steps.narration: Open Settings from the side bar.
steps.caption: 1. Open Settings

steps.narration: This row builds the subfolders. Each blue block is one piece of information — here, the sender, then the year, then the month.
steps.caption: Blue blocks = your subfolders

steps.narration: Click a block below to add another level, or the little cross on a block to remove one.
steps.caption: Add or remove blocks

steps.narration: This second builder is the file name itself — by default the document type, its date, and its reference number.
steps.caption: The file name pattern

steps.narration: Say you also want the sender's name in the filename —
steps.caption: 3. Add a block

steps.narration: — just click Issuer, and the live preview shows exactly where a document would be saved and what it'd be called.
steps.caption: Live preview updates as you go

steps.narration: Not sure? Reset to Default puts either builder back the way it started.
steps.caption: Reset to Default anytime

steps.narration: Now every document files itself neatly. Next: letting the easy ones file automatically.
steps.caption: Next: auto-filing
